messages:
support_julia: Hi team — customer Alice (alice_customer) reporting sharp p95/p99 latency increase after we onboarded model citrine-3 yesterday. She says API timeouts for long-context (>32k) requests jumped from ~600ms to 3–8s.

alice_customer: Confirming — noticed spikes in production from ~08:30 UTC yesterday after switching to citrine-3: many chat completions time out and sometimes partial stream then disconnects.

support_julia: Thanks Alice. Can you share a sample request/headers (no PII) and the exact endpoint you hit? Also are you on Hosted or Dedicated?

alice_customer: Hosted. Example payload: `curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H \"Authorization: Bearer X\" -d '{\"model\":\"citrine-3\",\"input\": \"<~32k tokens>...\"}'` — returns 504 or stalls streaming.

mike_ml: Filing an ML triage note: citation: citrine-3 -> tokenizer change + longer KV chain. Early hypothesis: new BPE merges increased average token length for CJK mix and triggered slowpath in our tokenizer and extra KV cache churn.

raj_runtime: On runtime side I see elevated tail latency on nodes serving citrine-3 in us-west-2 cluster around 08:20–09:40 UTC. p50 ~ 400ms, p95 ~ 1.2s, p99 ~ 4.7s. Logs show repeated KV cache misses and re-syncs for big seqs.

support_julia: Noted. Can you paste the relevant snippet of the runtime logs?

raj_runtime: ```
[08:22:13] req=abc123 model=citrine-3 seq_tokens=30720 kv_cache_miss=true kv_repair=true route=us-west-2 node=gpu-12
[08:22:13] warn: kv_repair triggered, fetching prefix snapshot, duration=1.1s
[08:22:14] info: streaming chunk sent, tokens=512
[08:22:17] error: downstream stream disconnect, code=EPIPE
```

mike_ml: I also repro'd locally. Under longcontext (30k–40k) the tokenizer returns a 1.3x larger token count for certain multilingual inputs vs previous model variants, which pushes us into different batching behavior and larger KV cache updates.

sre_ian: Ops note: we throttled citrine-3 to reduced concurrency at 09:05 UTC to protect cluster. That dropped errors but tail latency remained higher than baseline.

support_julia: Customer wants ETA + mitigation. Alice, can you tolerate a temporary fallback to citrine-2 for long documents?

alice_customer: We can fallback for now but need citrine-3 features (finer summarization). Ideally a fix or config change that keeps citrine-3 for short requests and falls back for >16k tokens.

mike_ml: Action plan: 1) Reproduce and capture tokenizer tokenization diffs for affected inputs. 2) Add a routing rule to split requests by client-side length and route >16k to citrine-2 or a compatible variant. 3) Patch runtime to avoid full KV snapshot fetch on transient misses (fast-stall vs full-repair). 4) Quick hotfix: reduce citrine-3 default max_batch_size and enable aggressive prefix caching.

raj_runtime: I can implement routing rule and reduce max_batch_size per-model as a hotfix. Rolling to canary now.

deploy-bot: deploy initiated by raj_runtime: patch/route-hotfix -> canary (2 nodes) (started at 10:12 UTC)

raj_runtime: Canary metrics after 20m: p95 down from 1.2s to 750ms, p99 down from 4.7s to 1.5s for canary nodes. However, overall cluster still shows some spikes — likely due to ongoing KV repair traffic.

mike_ml: For the tokenizer itself I prepared a short diff that avoids one heavy normalization pass that doubled byte-escape handling for certain emoji sequences. That reduces token expansion for those inputs. I propose we roll tokenizer change to citrine-3 v1.0.1.

sre_ian: Before we release tokenizer patch, we should run load test with mixed lengths and enable the new prefix-only KV repair flow to avoid full snapshot fetch. I'll schedule an isolated canary in us-west-2 with traffic replay from Alice's recent traces.

support_julia: Communicating back to Alice: we're enabling a temporary routing fallback and already seeing improved latencies on canary nodes. Asking if she can switch a small % of traffic to the canary endpoint for validation.

alice_customer: Willing to send 10% to canary for 2 hours. Appreciate the temporary rollback rules.

raj_runtime: Rolling routing rule to customer ID scope -> now serving 10% of alice_customer traffic to canary nodes (10:45 UTC). Will monitor.

deploy-bot: rollout update: route-rule alice_customer -> canary 10% (completed at 10:46 UTC)

raj_runtime: After 90 minutes: canary p99 ~1.2s, error rate down 82% for Alice. Rolling patch to reduce max_batch_size cluster-wide for citrine-3 by 25% to reduce batching pressure.

mike_ml: Tokenizer patch ready — small change, regression test included. I'll open PR and request fast-track review.

sre_ian: Postmortem next steps: - finalize kv-repair fast-path (avoid snapshot) - deploy tokenizer v1.0.1 after canary passes - add model-level routing rule toggle for customers - add doc for long-context degradation modes and recommended client-side length checks

support_julia: Customer update: thanks — we'll keep 10% on canary while we monitor and plan a gradual increase once tokenizer patch + KV fast-path are live. ETA: routing + batching changes already done; tokenizer patch + KV fast-path target EOD UTC tomorrow.

alice_customer: Thanks team — 10% canary is working, latency much better. We'll keep monitoring on our end and report any regressions.

mike_ml: Filed internal ticket ML-2238 for tokenizer patch, runtime ticket RUNTIME-1184 for kv-repair fast-path and RUNTIME-1185 for per-model batch config.

support_julia: Closing loop in support: tracking tickets ML-2238, RUNTIME-1184, RUNTIME-1185. Will reopen if anything else crops up. :thumbsup:
